message.content: {"summary":"You have built a clear, well-referenced case for a single sun-synchronous Earth-observation spacecraft, and your STK access results and ground-track evidence are a real strength. The main gaps are technical accuracy and closure: the RAAN rationale and Vega E timeline need correcting, the end-of-life strategy is unresolved, and the reference list has missing and inappropriate sources. Fixing these would lift the report substantially.","next_steps":["Resolve your end-of-life strategy in the Mission Duration and EOL section: quantify uncontrolled decay at 600 km against the 25-year guideline, remove the unsupported burn-up claim, choose passive or active disposal, and make the manoeuvre statements in the Orbit section consistent with it.","Correct the orbit design: remove the link between RAAN and the launch site and justify the RAAN from mission requirements. State the orbital period and epoch, and add swath, ground sample distance and revisit calculations to support your daily reef imaging claim and altitude choice. Also address the azimuth and performance penalties of launching from Kourou into a 97.8 degree retrograde orbit.","Tidy the launch timeline and references: align the Vega E first-launch date and the 2021 alternatives with your 2025 plan, replace the Wikipedia source, add entries for [49] to [74], and resolve the duplicate use of [10]. Then number all tables and figures and check every in-text citation against the reference list."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your primary mission, the rationale for it and your choice of a single spacecraft are clearly explained and supported by references, which is a solid base. To reach the next level, name the operator and specific customers rather than listing possible agencies, and support your comparison with constellation-based Earth-observation systems using credible, appropriate sources.","C2":"Your STK access results, ground track and inclination-altitude plot provide good visual evidence. Key corrections are needed: RAAN is wrongly tied to the launch site, the Vega E date conflicts with your 2025 launch, and altitude reasoning is contradictory without a swath or ground sample distance calculation. Your end-of-life strategy is unresolved, and decay is not checked against the 25-year guideline.","C3":"You reach some sensible conclusions, notably the risk of relying on a launch vehicle not yet built and the need for a fallback. However, the conclusion mainly restates the design. To reach the next level, draw specific conclusions from your evidence, such as whether the mission duration and end-of-life approach are adequate, and what your contact-time results mean for operations.","C4":"Your report follows a clear, logical structure with headings that guide the reader. To improve presentation, replace the Wikipedia source, add the missing entries for citations [49] to [74], and resolve the duplicate use of [10]. Number your tables and figures consistently, complete the truncated drag-sail sentence, and correct the duplicated access period numbering in the Ground Control section."}}
